evidence.note: Read run_tests.sh and its Python scoring files, then summarized filter.json test counts — learned how pass/fail is judged and the corpus scale before writing any compiler code.

Sampled each suite (c-testsuite, wacc, gcc-torture), checked env/tool versions and available headers, computed wacc chapter distribution and gcc-torture feature/include frequency — systematic corpus characterization that produced an evidence-based feature-priority ordering.

The feature-staged task list (lexer, preprocessor, types, SysV-ABI codegen incl. structs/varargs/floats, driver) is derived from the corpus survey rather than assumption, showing orientation fed design.

On struct-return failures, drilled deeply into SysV struct-return ABI (small vs large structs, register vs memory return), inspecting emitted assembly and reference behavior — verifying ABI details against reality mid-build.

Sustained drill-downs into exact constructs (complex numbers, vector types, nested functions), building precise models of each corner and feeding them back into codegen — treating the suites as an evolving spec, not a one-time read.

reasoning: The agent's opening is a systematic characterization of the corpus (scoring mechanism, per-suite feature sampling, chapter/feature-frequency distributions, available headers) that yields an evidence-derived feature-priority ordering — squarely the level-8 anchor. It then sustains investigation throughout, repeatedly drilling into the exact failing C construct and verifying ABI corners (struct return, stack alignment, promotions, complex/vector semantics) against reality and feeding them back into design — the level-10 behavior. Because up-front ABI verification was partly discovered iteratively rather than fully confirmed before use, I place the observed level at 9 rather than 10.
